name: Burak
world_status: accessible description is silent on stress

earlier_scan.source_named: Othaniel, Nlabephee Kefas. 2017. A phonological comparative study of the Jen language cluster; Norton & Othaniel 2020, The Jen language cluster (wordlists).
earlier_scan.note: Only comparative-phonology works cover Burak; neither found online in fetchable form; suprasegmentals likely tone-focused.

sources.citation: Harley, Matthew. 2020. Aspects of the phonology and morphosyntax of Kyak, an Adamawa language. Language in Africa 1(3): 373–404. (sister language Kyak/Bambuka, not Burak)
sources.access_detail: copy on file; access check: open copy online (also: harvard online access (harvardkey))
sources.note: Describes Kyak (bamb1262), a Bikwin sister language: tone-marked throughout; the words stress/accent do not occur in the text layer. Burak mentioned only in the classification sentence (p. 374 area: 'comprising Burak-Loo, Maghdi and Mak, and a southern subgroup'). Not a Burak source.

sources.citation: Adelberger, Jörg & Blench, Roger. 2026. The peopling of the Muri Mountains, Northern Nigeria: evidence from linguistics and ethnography. Afrikanistik-Aegyptologie-Online. doi:10.18716/ojs/aaeo/2026_12031
sources.note: Ethnography and settlement history; §3.2.3.6 Burak (p. 18) gives population (c. 7,500, 1991 census), clans and migrations; no phonology, no stress.

sources.citation: Norton, Russell & Othaniel, Nlabephee. 2020. The Jen language cluster: A comparative analysis of wordlists. Language in Africa 1(3): 17–99. doi:10.37892/2686-8946-2020-1-3-17-99
sources.note: Nothing. The paper is a comparative wordlist study of ten Jen varieties (Burak included). §3.3 Tone (p. 43): 'High, mid, low, falling and rising tones were noted' for the cluster; Burak forms carry H/M/L tone marks throughout (Table 20 p. 44 gives Burak *L reflexes gɑ̀b 'answer', kɔ̀klɛ̀ 'bark'); §3.4 breathy voice. The words stress/accent/prominence do not occur anywhere in the 83 pages (grep of full text layer).

sources.citation: Harley, Matthew. 2019. Aspects of Kyak phonology, morphology and syntax. Slides, First Adamawa Conference, Mainz.
sources.note: Kyak, not Burak; no stress statement (Burak appears only as a column header in one cognate table).

sources.citation: Norton, Russell & Othaniel, Nlabephee. 2019. The Jen cluster: comparative analysis of wordlists. Slides, First Adamawa Conference, Mainz, September 2019.
sources.note: Nothing on stress; tone-marked comparative tables (Burak column) and slides on vowel nasalisation; no prosody statement beyond tone diacritics.

sources.citation: Adamawa Languages Project (Mainz), Bikwin-Jen group page (Kleinewillinghöfer 2017), https://www.blogs.uni-mainz.de/fb07-adamawa/bikwin-jen-group/
sources.note: Classification note (Burak and Loo mutually intelligible variants of one language; no trace of noun classes); names Othaniel 2017 as the phonological comparative study; nothing on stress.

sources.citation: Kleinewillinghöfer, Ulrich. 2014. Adamawa (classification overview slides, 04.02.2014). Mainz, 26 pp.
sources.note: Classification only; Bikwin-Jen mentioned on one slide; nothing on Burak phonology or stress.

sources.citation: Kleinewillinghöfer, Ulrich. 1995/2015. Bikwin-Jen — Comparative Wordlist (Swadesh 100). Mainz: Adamawa Languages Project, 13 pp.
sources.note: Wordlist only (BU = Burak [Ɓʋʋrak] column); forms carry tone diacritics in a legacy font; no statement on stress or tone.

sources.citation: Glottolog 5.x languoid page bura1271 (Hammarström et al.)
sources.note: Bibliographic record only: lists Bennett 1983, Boyd & Pasch 1988, Norton & Othaniel 2020, Kleinewillinghöfer 1996 (p. 96) and Kleinewillinghöfer 2020 (p. 224) as classification refs; no grammar or phonology reference for Burak.

sources.citation: Kleinewillinghöfer, Ulrich. n.d. Bikwin-Jen: Pronouns and Numbers 1-10. Mainz: Adamawa Languages Project, 1 p.

sources.note: No phonology section; cites Ethnologue, Blench 2019 Atlas, Adelberger 2024 and Adelberger & Blench 2026.

sources.citation: Norton, Russell & Othaniel, Nlabephee. 2018. Ten alphabets from one: A phonological comparative study of the Jen cluster. Presentation to the Jos Linguistics Circle.

sources.note: Orthography-oriented phonology overview of all ten Jen varieties by the same authors; may contain per-language tone/prosody summaries that the 2020 wordlist paper omits.

sources.citation: Othaniel, Nlabephee Kefas. 2017. A phonological comparative study of the Jen language cluster. Bukuru/Jos: Theological College of Northern Nigeria, 83 pp. (B.A. dissertation per Norton & Othaniel 2020; M.A. per Glottolog)

sources.note: The only work devoted to the phonology of the cluster including Burak; a per-language phonology chapter is the most likely place for a suprasegmental (tone, and possibly stress) statement on Burak. Named by the earlier scan and by the Mainz Bikwin-Jen page.
